To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the incidence of training is positively related to the overall educational level and the financial input of the educational system, whereas the returns to training seem to depend on the quality of secondary education.
training incidence varies according to the level and the stratification of education, whereas returns vary according to the quality of secondary education.

the returns to training vary according to the quality of the education system and that this variation is related to the stratification of secondary education and the financial input of the system of initial education.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether there is a link between institutional factors of skill formation and training and the incidence and returns to training.
the question of whether the institutional factors of the education and training system are important determinants of the level of training incidence, the returns of training, or both.
the relationship between the initial skill formation of individuals, the training of employees and the returns of this training.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the institutional framework of initial skill formation is a key determinant of the training system in terms of incidence and returns.
countries with high levels of educational expenditure and a high share of secondary school graduates are also likely to have higher rates of training participation and higher training returns.
training is a means for individuals to cope with skill demands that are not met by the educational system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a strong link between initial skill formation and the provision of further training, but the link between the two is not straightforward.
the system of initial training is an important determinant of both the level of training participation and the returns to training.
the quality of initial skill formation is a key factor for the provision of training, its returns and inequality in the labour market.
The main takeaway from our work is that
initial education systems and their stratification are crucial factors in explaining country-level differences in training and its returns.

initial skill formation is a crucial determinant of the incidence and returns of employee training, and that the institutional setup of education is a major factor in explaining the variation in training incidence across Europe.
the institutional context of initial skill formation is an important factor for understanding the relationship between employee skills and productivity.
